title: Your first checkmates
intro: Win with a queen, or with two rooks: the finishing patterns every player needs.

lessons.title: Mate with king and queen
lessons.summary: Push the king to the edge, then finish it, without stalemate.

steps.text: A queen cannot checkmate alone. Push the enemy king to the edge of the board, then bring your own king close to cover its escape squares.
Your king guards the squares in front of the black king. Now the queen checks along the edge, and there is no way out.
Your turn: checkmate with the queen.
steps.hint: Your king already covers f7, g7 and h7. Check along the top row, or right next to the king where your king protects the queen.
steps.ifWrong: Not mate. Give a check the king cannot escape.

steps.hint: Your king covers a7 and b7. Check along the top row.
steps.ifWrong: Not mate. Find the check that leaves no escape.

steps.text: Careful now. Find the checkmate, and do not let it become stalemate.
steps.hint: Give check. A move that takes every square away without check is stalemate.
steps.ifWrong: Not mate. The king must be in check with no escape.

feedback.c1c7: Stalemate! Black has no legal move but is not in check, so the game is a draw. Always give check when you take the last squares.

lessons.title: The rook ladder
lessons.summary: Two rooks walk the king to the edge.

steps.text: Two rooks mate easily. One rook guards a row so the king cannot come back; the other gives check on the next row. Then they swap jobs, like climbing a ladder.
The rook on b6 guards the 6th row. Check with the other rook to push the king up, then checkmate.
steps.hint: First a check on the 7th row, then a check on the 8th.
steps.ifWrong: Keep the ladder going: check on the next row up, while the other rook guards.
steps.ifRight: Checkmate! The two rooks took turns.

steps.text: Mate in one with the rooks.
steps.hint: One rook already guards the 7th row.
steps.ifWrong: Not mate. Check on the top row while the other rook guards.

steps.text: The ladder works sideways too. Mate in one.
steps.hint: The rook on b2 guards the b-file.
steps.ifWrong: Not mate. Check on the a-file while the other rook guards b.
